item.title: Beyond Self-Similarity: Reconciling X-Ray Scaling Relations in Galaxy Clusters and Groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.02719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scaling relations hold among observed quantities that describe the thermodynamic properties of the gas in galaxy clusters and groups. However, observed data show systematic departures from the self-similar model's baseline predictions, particularly in lower-mass systems. I show that the observed departures from self-similar predictions can be efficiently described by two physical quantities modeled with power laws: the gas mass fraction $f_g$ and the temperature variation $f_T$. Using a wide range of published X-ray scaling relations, this study conducts an MCMC-based meta-analysis to constrain the temperature- and redshift-dependence of the meta-parameters $f_g$ and $f_T$ and calibrate the model. These calibrations indicate that, while the gas mass fraction does not show significant evolution with cosmic time, it decreases significantly with decreasing halo mass. On the other hand, the temperature variation shows a mild positive increase with both mass and redshift. Overall, modeling the departures from the self-similar model with $\{f_g, f_T\}$ drastically improves predictive accuracy, reducing the number of scaling relations in $>3\sigma$ ($>5 \sigma$) tension from 49 (36) percent under the self-similar scenario to just 11 (3) percent (four and one out of 39, respectively) that might be identified for their peculiarity. Moreover, modeling through this generalized framework allows for an extended discussion of the expected slopes and redshift evolution for several X-ray scaling laws, including the new quantity $Y_{LGT0} = L^{-1} M_g^2 T^{a_L}$, a proxy for the cluster's volume that is independent of $f_g$ and $f_T$ by construction, and is predicted to scale directly with mass with a well-defined redshift evolution ($M \sim Y_{LGT0} f_g^0 f_T^0 E_z^2$), as validated against hydrodynamical simulations and observational constraints.

item.title: Nuclear Millimeter Continuum Emission in Radio-Quiet Active Galactic Nuclei: an ALMA Spectral and Variability Study
item.description: arXiv:2610.30286v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unresolved millimeter (mm) emission is observed in radio-quiet (RQ) Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN), but its physical origin remains debated. Self-absorbed synchrotron emission from the compact X-ray corona is one of the leading candidates. Previous support for this coronal synchrotron origin has mainly been based on variability and spectral indices in a few RQ AGN, with a lack of (quasi-)simultaneous broadband data for larger samples. We present Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) observations of nine nearby ($z \sim 0.008-0.064$) RQ AGN, obtained quasi-simultaneously at 100, 145, and 233 GHz. Based on power-law fits to the spectral energy distributions, we measure millimeter spectral indices ranging from $-0.05^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$ to $0.88^{+0.12}_{-0.11}$. Furthermore, across two 100 GHz observing epochs per source, separated by $4-11$ days, we detect flux density variability of $30-56$% (>$3\sigma$ significance level) in three out of nine sources. Spectral slopes alone are insufficient to constrain the origin of the millimeter emission; however, the observed short-timescale variability and inferred brightness temperature values are consistent with a non-thermal emission mechanism arising from a compact emitting region with a size of $R_{\rm mm}< 10^3 - 10^4 R_{\rm g}$, such as the corona or a compact jet. Furthermore, we find a clear correlation between the 100/233 GHz and X-ray flux in our sample, and establish a new linear correlation between 145 GHz and X-ray emission.

item.title: The Edge of the Warm Corona in Active Galactic Nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2611.12595v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A model of warm, dissipative corona on top of an accretion disk is investigated, to explain the soft X-ray excess (SXE) emission observed in active galactic nuclei (AGN). The final ray-traced spectrum, computed through photoionization code with Comptonization, accounts for both: emitted and reflected components. As a result, the strength of the SXE depends on the radial extend of the warm corona, i.e., its outer edge. We show that the radial transition from warm corona to disk atmosphere is governed by line cooling. By moving away from a central black hole Compton cooling is gradually replaced by line cooling, and the temperature drops sharply in vertical direction at a narrow iron ionization front, where iron ions Fe \textsc{xxv}--Fe \textsc{xxvi} recombine to Fe \textsc{xvii}. Notably, this transition takes place at a particular value of internal heating $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-23}$ erg cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$, regardless of the Eddington ratio. We show, that at the given metal abundance, the SXE emitting area is larger for a higher accretion rate, in agreement with recent findings in changing look AGN. The overall emission spectrum from a warm corona is featureless, and the only iron K$_{\alpha}$ line comes from a reflection. The line is stronger and more gravitationally distorted for a lower accretion rate, which is a direct result of the size of the warm corona. Furthermore, by increasing the iron abundance, the iron ionization front moves closer towards black hole, and a stronger iron line complex is emitted locally.
